rationale: Kani bounded model checking proves PayloadTooLarge returned before any Vec allocation on hostile input. Harness must use kani::any() for header bytes and payload_len where len > max. Current kani_record_payload_len.rs uses hardcoded magic (0x5650424C) — new harness needed that uses kani::any() for all header fields.
bounds: payload_len ∈ [max+1, u32::MAX], max ∈ [1, u32::MAX], magic ∈ u32
assumptions: header bytes are arbitrary 60 bytes from kani::any()
expected_evidence: Kani: proof completes with PayloadTooLarge returned before any Vec creation
leak_prevention: kani::any::<[u8; 60]>() for header; kani::any::<u32>() for max_payload_len where max > 0; kani::any::<u32>() for payload_len where len > max

rationale: Kani exhausts all input lengths (0, 1-59, 60, 61+) proving no panic. Covers truncate-at-60 boundary. kani_codec.rs H1-H4 provide partial coverage but use hardcoded fixed bytes — this harness uses kani::any() for arbitrary length slices.
assumptions: arbitrary bytes from kani::any()
expected_evidence: Kani: proof completes with no panic branches reachable
leak_prevention: kani::any::<[u8; N]>() for N ∈ {0, 1, 30, 59, 60, 61, 100, 200}; kani::any::<u32>() for magic and max

rationale: Kani proves bytes[60..60+payload_len] slice is bounded by max_payload_len after budget gate passes. Existing kani_record_payload_len.rs proves header-level check; this proves payload-level slice bounds.

rationale: Kani proves checked_add overflow check at payload.rs line 66 prevents wraparound. When 60 + payload_len overflows usize, checked_add returns None → UnexpectedEof before slice access.
